title: How to pick between packs, and when core already does it

questions.q: What is the first rung of the ladder?
options: How many stars does it have?
questions.why: Each pack adds code at every start. Check whether you need one.

questions.q: You want plain perturbed-attention guidance. Which do you try first?
options: A new pack with more stars
questions.why: Core has it. The pack answers a different need, such as token perturbation.

questions.q: A pack's README claims 1.45× speed. What is that worth?
options: A reason to try it and measure, on a baseline of your own
Proof that core is slower everywhere
questions.answer: A reason to try it and measure, on a baseline of your own
questions.why: It's the author's number on the author's graph.

questions.q: A pack has a good idea but patches every job. What fits best?
options: Borrow the idea and write your own
questions.answer: Borrow the idea and write your own
questions.why: Ideas are reusable, and the side effects stay in the pack.

questions.q: Why do you write down what core lacks as one sentence?
options: If you can't name the gap, you don't need a pack yet
questions.answer: If you can't name the gap, you don't need a pack yet
questions.why: It stops a vague want from becoming a new dependency.

questions.q: Why not run two step caches on one model?
options: Both patch the same forward path, and results can change with no error
They double the speed, which is too fast
questions.answer: Both patch the same forward path, and results can change with no error
